minutes.headline: Charter Review Committee took no votes and debated a public survey versus a public hearing
minutes.summary: The committee met without several members and without a super majority, so no votes were taken. A cemetery commission representative dropped off a proposal to add a missing word to the charter. Members then discussed the finance and town manager sections, the February meeting schedule, the town meeting timeline, and whether to survey the public or hold a hearing.

public_comment.topic: A resident said she will recommend a charter change and that public opinion counts equally; the chair said she need not wait for the public hearing.
A speaker new to civic involvement said she had been told she should have no voice, and argued the committee should seek input from all residents.

decisions.decision: The chair will circulate the cemetery commission's printout to the committee and take it up as an agenda item at the next meeting.
The town manager session is set for the 24th of January; the February 7 meeting will sort items into no change, stylistic change and substantive change.
Tentative added meetings on February 7 and 21 were discussed alongside the regular February 14 and 28 meetings; a hearing venue was to be checked.

what_happened.line: The Charter Review Committee took no votes because members were absent and a super majority was not present.
The chair will circulate a cemetery commission proposal to add a missing word to the charter and take it up as an agenda item at the next meeting.
The committee discussed the finance and town manager sections of the charter and compared them with other towns' charters.
Tentative added meetings on February 7 and 21 were discussed, with the regular February 14 and 28 meetings; a hearing venue was still to be checked.
The town manager session is set for January 24; the February 7 meeting will sort items into no change, stylistic change and substantive change.

why_it_matters: The charter is the town's governing document, so changes the committee proposes could later reach residents as a Town Meeting or ballot vote.
The committee had not settled whether to survey residents or hold a public hearing, which decides how and when residents can weigh in on proposed changes.
